correctness.rationale: On the calibrated state interval, Y=N^beta satisfies Y'=beta(a-u)Y-beta b. The explicit integrating-factor formula is decreasing under cumulative-effort domination while both solutions are positive. For equal totals the terminal prefactor is common and strict ordering follows from the integral whenever the continuous effort curves differ. For U<=g(N0), the constant-cap trajectory never decreases below N0 and bounds all competitors below. For U>g(N0), the maximal-rate trajectory decreases strictly to Nc. Spending less than its cost gives a front-loaded trajectory that runs out of effort above Nc, then grows; cumulative ordering rules out any competitor reaching Nc. At the minimal cost, terminal strictness forces the same initial maximal-rate pulse up to the first hit. Integration along that pulse gives the displayed budget integral and its strict monotonicity; substitution near U=g(N0) gives the stated logarithmic rate and constant. The deadline and strict-crossing conclusions follow from trajectory comparison and Nc>Nref. The pulse expressions presuppose U>0; at U=0 the only admissible control is identically zero and the ordering is trivial. No positive-state claim beyond calibration was used.
residual_risks: Finite checks corroborate the formulas only; the measurable-control result follows from the analytic comparisons.

value.rationale: For a previously motivated deterministic takeoff law the result separates a rate-cap obstruction that no total effort can fix from the minimum sufficient finite budget. It also quantifies the singular cost near the feasibility boundary, identifies the unique measurable optimal schedule, and distinguishes threshold access from crossing. Those are useful exact control predictions beyond solving an affine equation for a prechosen constant intervention.
residual_risks: Integrated proportional loss is not headcount or monetary cost; the result does not establish actual population extinction, claims below calibration, or applicability to stochastic or congested systems.
